source: NRDC (2015), Home Idle Load: Devices Wasting Huge Amounts of Electricity When Not in Active Use, Table 3: top 20 idle loads, average idle load per device across a 10-home audit sample.

devices.name: Set-top box / DVR
devices.tip: Turn off 'quick start' and use the deep standby setting, or put it on a timer plug overnight.

devices.name: TV
devices.tip: Disable instant-on / voice wake, or switch off at the wall with the soundbar.

devices.name: Broadband modem
devices.tip: Usually worth keeping on. An all-in-one router + modem saves a box.

devices.name: Desktop computer (asleep or off)
devices.tip: Check that sleep actually happens; a power strip removes the off-mode draw.

devices.name: Security / alarm system
devices.tip: Needed. Check the panel is not also powering an old phone line box.

devices.name: Audio / video gear (soundbar, AV receiver)
devices.tip: Put the whole TV corner on one switched strip.

devices.name: Laptop charger left plugged in
devices.tip: Unplug when the battery is full.

devices.name: Printer / fax / copier
devices.tip: Most homes print rarely: unplug it.

devices.name: Wi-Fi router
devices.tip: Keep it, but retire extra extenders you no longer need.

devices.name: Other networking (extenders, switches, hubs)
devices.tip: Each smart-home hub draws power 24/7; consolidate where you can.

devices.name: Cordless phone base
devices.tip: If nobody uses the landline, unplug the base.

devices.name: Lights left on 24/7 (porch, night lights)
devices.tip: A timer or dusk sensor fixes this for good.

devices.name: Aquarium equipment
devices.tip: Pumps must run; LED lighting and an efficient heater cut the rest.

devices.name: Fan left running
devices.tip: Bathroom extractor or bedroom fan forgotten on? It shows up as a raised floor.

devices.name: Hot water recirculation pump
devices.tip: Fit a timer or demand switch so it only runs when needed.

devices.name: Pond pump / filter
devices.tip: Needed for fish, but an efficient pump can halve the draw.

devices.name: Fridge-freezer (average while cycling)
devices.tip: Estimate from typical energy-label use of 150 to 450 kWh a year. Older or American-style units sit at the top of that range.
